name: Hạ Long Bay
summary: A bay of nearly 2,000 limestone islands rising from green water. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the great landscapes of Asia.

hero.alt: Limestone islands in Hạ Long Bay

eras.label: Long ago
eras.title: Islands from the sea
eras.text: The islands are the tops of limestone hills drowned by the sea. Their rock, caves and fossils record hundreds of millions of years of the Earth's history, and their steep sides have been carved by waves into arches and notches.

image.file: Halong Bay, Rock formations in fog.jpg

eras.label: c. 1900
eras.title: The "Baie d'Along"
eras.text: Under French rule, the bay became famous in postcards and travel books as the "Baie d'Along". Steamers took visitors from Hải Phòng to see its caves and islands.

image.alt: An old view of the bay

eras.title: World Heritage
eras.text: UNESCO listed Hạ Long Bay as a World Heritage Site for its outstanding beauty, and in 2000 added its geological value.

eras.title: Joined with Cát Bà
eras.text: The World Heritage Site was extended to include the Cát Bà archipelago in neighbouring Hải Phòng, creating one protected landscape of more than 1,000 square kilometres.

eras.label: Today
eras.title: Life on the water
eras.text: Most families of the floating fishing villages moved ashore in the 2010s, but a few floating houses remain. Cruise boats now carry visitors between the islands and into the caves.

image.file: Lang Chai Floating Village-Halong Bay Vietnam-Andres Larin.jpg
image.alt: A floating village in the bay

story.title: Where the dragon came down
story.narration: Hạ Long means 'where the dragon descends'. The legend says that when Vietnam was threatened by invaders from the sea, the Jade Emperor sent a mother dragon and her children down from heaven to help. They spat out jewels and jade, which fell into the sea and became a wall of islands that wrecked the enemy ships. The dragons liked the peaceful bay so much that they stayed on earth. The mother came down at Hạ Long, and her children at Bái Tử Long, the bay 'where the children bowed to their mother'.

story.title: The stakes of Bạch Đằng
story.narration: Twice in Vietnam's history, invaders were destroyed on the Bạch Đằng River, which flows into the sea just west of the bay. In 938 Ngô Quyền had wooden stakes tipped with iron driven into the riverbed. At high tide, his boats lured the enemy fleet in. When the tide went out, the ships were caught on the hidden stakes and destroyed. In 1288, General Trần Hưng Đạo used the same trick against the fleet of the Mongol Yuan dynasty. Some of the stakes have been found by archaeologists in the riverbanks.

story.title: Caves inside the islands
story.narration: Many of the islands are hollow. Sửng Sốt, the 'Surprise Cave', opens into huge chambers full of stalactites. Thiên Cung, the 'Heavenly Palace', is decorated with rock formations that guides compare to dragons, fairies and flowers. Fishermen once sheltered from storms in these caves. Today visitors also explore the bay by kayak, paddling into lagoons that can only be reached through low tunnels at low tide.

story.title: Among the islands

video.alt: Video of limestone islands rising from calm water in Hạ Long Bay, with boats in the distance

story.narration: A short clip of Hạ Long Bay, filmed from the water in December 2024. Steep limestone islands rise straight out of calm sea, and tourist boats move slowly between them. There are around sixteen hundred islands and islets in the bay, most of them uninhabited and covered in forest.

guide.price: Bay entry ticket, plus a cruise. Day cruises last 4–8 hours, or you can stay overnight on a boat.

hours.notes: Approximate. Day boats run in daylight; overnight cruises stay on the bay.

do: Book cruises with licensed operators, and check what the price includes.
Wear a life jacket on small boats and kayaks.
Bring a jacket in winter. It is cold and misty on the water.
Visit at least one cave and one viewpoint.
dont: Throw rubbish or food into the water.
Touch stalactites or write on the cave walls.
Swim away from the official beaches.

tips.title: Seafood
tips.text: Try chả mực (fried squid cakes), and fresh seafood at Hạ Long's harbour restaurants.

tips.title: Getting there
tips.text: About 2–2.5 hours from Hà Nội on the expressway. Cruises leave from Tuần Châu and Bãi Cháy.

tips.title: Best views
tips.text: Climb to the top of Ti Tốp island, or ride the cable car to Ba Đèo hill in Hạ Long city.
